predecessors.name: Empire of Brazil
predecessors.text: the whole country, after the coup of 15 November 1889

ledger.x: 15 November 1889: a military coup overthrows the monarchy and Brazil becomes a republic.
1903: Brazil occupies Acre.
17 November 1903: the occupation of Acre ends in annexation by the Treaty of Petrópolis, 'signed on November 17, 1903'.
17 November 1903: Bolivia cedes Acre to Brazil.
17 November 1903: in exchange Brazil cedes 'over 3,000 km2 of Brazilian territory between the Abuna River and Madeira River' to Bolivia.
15 June 1904: the Pirara arbitration.
1928: the Tratado de Límites y Navegación Fluvial.
1928: Brazil gains 1 cell (253 km2) near Tabatinga from Cliopatria's Peru shape; no page dates or explains it.
October 1930: 'An armed revolution in 1930 ended the First Republic and brought Getúlio Vargas to power.'
1932: Cliopatria's label becomes 'Unitary State of Brazil' (1932-1945); the Brazil page does not use the name.
1936: Cliopatria's shape adds 2 cells from its Paraguay shape (and 4 from Bolivia's) around Porto Murtinho; none of the pages opened dates a frontier change.
1936: the other 4 of the 6 cells come from Cliopatria's Bolivia shape (the Chaco claim).
1936: 1 cell (253 km2) passes to Paraguay in Cliopatria's shape.
1937: 'The 1937 coup d'état resulted in the cancellation of the 1938 election and formalized Vargas as dictator, beginning the Estado Novo era.'
1945: Vargas 'was swiftly overthrown in another military coup'; 'Democracy was restored after Vargas' ousting in 1945'.
1960: the capital moves to Brasília, 'the new capital city of Brasília, inaugurated in 1960'.
April 1964: the government 'was deposed in April 1964 by a coup that resulted in a military dictatorship' that 'ruled until 1985'.
1967: Cliopatria's label becomes 'Federated Republic of Brazil'; the Brazil page does not mention a 1967 constitution.
1985: 'Civilians returned to power in 1985 when José Sarney assumed the presidency.'
5 October 1988: the current constitution is 'promulgated on 5 October 1988' and the last three territories become states ('Amapá and Roraima (which gained statehood)').

wars.name: Acre War
wars.outcome: Acrean victory: Bolivia surrendered Puerto Alonso on 24 January 1903; the Treaty of Petrópolis (17 November 1903) gave Brazil Acre (191,000 km2) for two million pounds, a railway pledge and over 3,000 km2 between the Abuna and Madeira.

wars.name: Constitutionalist Revolution
wars.outcome: Rising of São Paulo's oligarchy against the Vargas government; the page gives no territory, dates or outcome.

certainty.note: Amazon frontiers are unsettled: Acre is disputed with Bolivia and Peru until the Treaty of Petrópolis, and the Pirara region with British Guiana until the 1904 arbitration.
The Bolivian frontier is set by the Treaty of Petrópolis (1903), the Guyana frontier by the 1904 award modified in 1926 and marked 1932-1939, the Colombian frontier by the treaties of 1907 and 1928.
